title: Phase-one failure loop
statement: Let $E$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be an oracle with four indices and Boolean-word queries, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $s,w$ be natural numbers with $s\le w$. Let $i$ be a natural number with $i+1\le w$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a machine state satisfying the following conditions: $n,a,X,P,T,Z,C,Q,E$ are zero; its radius is $s$, width is $w$, and code bound is $2^w$; its source and target codes are less than $2^w$, its midpoint is at most $2^w$, and its level is $i+1$; its saved-endpoints stack is less than $2^{w(w-(i+1))}$ and its phase stack is less than $2^{w-(i+1)}$. Suppose also that $M<2^w$ and $M_2\le 2^w$. Starting at label $a1F$ with the source code replaced by the old midpoint $M$, the midpoint replaced by $M_2$, and the popped endpoint set to the old source code, the machine can reach label $loop$ with the midpoint increased from its original value by one and every other register equal to its value in $\mathrm{st}$. Every configuration strictly before the endpoint has all registers at most $2^{w^2}$ and satisfies the machine's validity condition.

the same state except that $M$ is increased by one. Every configuration before the
endpoint satisfies the guard with register bound $2^{w^2}$.
